Subject: Hosted API pricing qualification: monthly token volume & peak TPS

Hey Jared — thanks again for the call earlier. Quick recap and the three asks we discussed so we can put together a draft hosted-API quote: 

1) Expected monthly token volume (ballpark): can you confirm the monthly active usage we should size for? you mentioned pilot -> ramp to production.
2) Peak TPS (inference requests per second) at 95th percentile: this affects reserved capacity vs. burst pricing.
3) Target unit economics / budget: ballpark $/1M tokens you want to hit for a long-term contract.

From our side, items we noted: hosted API gives fastest time-to-value; we can include streaming and function-calling in the same plan. For capacity guidance – if you expect sustained peaks we can recommend a small dedicated pool during business hours and hosted for rest, but we'll price both.

Next steps: if you can reply with the two numbers (monthly tokens and peak TPS) and a high/low budget range by EOD tomorrow, I'll share a 3-month pilot pro-forma and a price range for hosted API + options. I've attached a one-page usage forecast template you can drop numbers into.

Thanks — Marissa

Thanks for the clear recap. Some numbers to use for sizing (these are approximate — we'll confirm with ops):

- Expected monthly token volume (steady state within 3–6 months): ~1.5B tokens / month (1,500,000,000). This assumes 200k MAUs with average 7.5k tokens/user across sessions.
- Peak TPS (95th percentile): ~8 TPS (spikes up to ~12 TPS for short windows during promotions).
- Budget / target unit economics: heading into procurement we'd like to be in the $40–$70 per 1M tokens range; ideal target for finance is ~$50 / 1M tokens for committed volumes.

Additional notes: compliance is important — we'll need SOC 2 attestation and standard data handling terms. Procurement timeline: target purchase decision late September; pilot kickoff early September.

Attaching a small export of our traffic profile for the last month. Happy to hop on another quick call if you want to walk the numbers.

—Jared
